# Independent proactive visual QA — issue #68

Issue: [Freeze and enforce one interchangeable frontend services boundary](https://github.com/dystrophyless/dubbed.ai/issues/68). Reviewer: **GPT-6.1 Sol, High**. Date: 2026-10-25, Windows / local Chromium. Snapshot: `9d286621177200fdb5f61ef963d0b6818ae76774`; issue snapshot in `../contracts/issue-68.md` says closed/accepted with zero discussion comments. Review only; no issue mutation or acceptance reversal performed.

## Verdict and scope

**One HIGH consumer-boundary defect, one MEDIUM recovery-contract/design gap, one LOW desktop usability concern.** The typed facade and representative architecture/conformance checks work in the bounded probes. However, AC-02's rule that unknown is not permission to duplicate a mutation is contradicted by a visible consumer: an uncertain checkout can start another operation under fresh identities. This is an integration defect at the facade consumption seam; it does not mean the mock adapter itself duplicated a committed operation.

This technical foundation has no standalone product screen. Its user job is to let domain screens show authoritative account/project/operation facts, keep uncertainty honest, and preserve safe recovery while adapters are interchangeable. The review therefore uses Projects for common unavailable/loading/conflict/unauthenticated results, Credits for an unknown mutation, and the actual bootstrap for explicit unavailable-real configuration. It is not a full audit of Projects, Credits, identity, or issue #76.

Only this issue folder was written. Existing dirty documentation, skills, screenshots and other reviewers' artifacts were preserved; see `worktree-boundary.txt`. `frontend-dirty-paths.txt` records the final frontend source dirty boundary. No product/spec edits, Git changes, dependency installation, real service, microphone or speaker access. Both port-4368 server sessions were stopped after their captures.

## Evidence and method

Fresh Chromium screenshots: **13**, isolated contexts, DPR 1, default browser zoom; audio muted and fake-device/fake-UI flags. `document.fonts.ready` was awaited before capture. Measured primary captures confirm Mabry Pro available. Every PNG in `screenshot-manifest.json` was opened with `view_image` and visually inspected. Full-page PNG height may exceed viewport; exact viewport is in logs.

`capture.cjs` uses the existing `e2e/harness/workspace-state-visual.html` controlled adapter harness, UI navigation and real consumer components. It supplies synthetic account/session/projects/credits; this is not a registered production account or live backend. Unavailable and loading responses are existing scenarios. Unknown is produced by `credits.startPurchase` returning `{status:'unknown', operationId}`. `injected.cjs` substitutes existing unavailable expressions only in the fetched harness module to return revision-conflict or unauthenticated for the selected list scenario; no product source is changed. Twelve expressions are replaced but only `projects.list` is invoked from those substituted branches in these probes; call journals are retained. `unknown-repeat.cjs` adds operation/initiation IDs to the existing call journal, then clicks checkout twice. It does not invent an adapter success.

For explicit real mode, Vite was restarted on the same private port with `VITE_SERVICE_ADAPTER=real`, and the actual `/` entry was opened in EN desktop/RU phone. This is real **configuration**, not an implemented real adapter. No external HTTP request was observed in these two captures; it is not universal transport/security proof.

Raw evidence: [metrics.json](metrics.json), [capture-log.json](capture-log.json), [injected-log.json](injected-log.json), [unknown-repeat-proof.json](unknown-repeat-proof.json), [real-config-log.json](real-config-log.json), [checks.txt](checks.txt), [screenshot manifest](screenshot-manifest.json).

## QA-68-01 — HIGH — Unknown checkout permits a replacement mutation with fresh identities

**Class:** confirmed implementation defect at a visible consumer of the facade. **Affected:** AC-02, shared unknown/reconciliation invariant; Flow 12 purchase initiation. **Evidence:** confirmed by browser call trace plus source; screenshot alone does not prove operation identity.

Reproduce with `capture.cjs` unknown scenario, or run `unknown-repeat.cjs` while mock Vite is on port 4368. On Credits click **Start mock checkout**; adapter returns unknown. Observe the unconfirmed notice and **Check payment status**, then click **Start mock checkout** again. Expected: preserve unresolved intent and reconcile it, without creating a new initiation/operation. Actual: a second `credits.startPurchase` call has a new operation ID and initiation ID; no `operations.resolve` appears between calls.

Exact trace from `unknown-repeat-proof.json`:

- First: operation `aabe1705-4553-4096-9607-c965898054d1`, initiation `5e859bf2-7a34-42d5-89b1-c8444003b8b5`.
- Second: operation `028d4bc0-e470-43a9-b8b6-dce26ef6ecad`, initiation `35b60bac-5cc3-428a-932a-62bf87de6191`.

Cause: `src/features/credits/CreditsScreen.tsx:582-585` fences only an intent with a known `purchase.state === 'pending'`. Unknown start has neither a purchase nor purchase state; lines 587-597 create and persist fresh IDs. Lines 622-625 record unknown, while the button disabled expression at line 819 checks only an active action or a known pending purchase. The existing `retryStart` path at 630-661 preserves IDs, but the separate enabled start bypasses it. Shared contract `00-shared-contract.md:652` explicitly says unknown/pending is not permission for a blind replacement purchase.

User impact: an uncertain payment initiation can be displaced locally and a second distinct intent issued. This mock probe does **not** establish real payment collection or a duplicate charge. The risk is precisely loss of replay/reconciliation safety promised by this foundation.

Scoped recommendation: gate every start action on any unresolved intent, route the user to reconciliation, and retain original operation/initiation IDs until the first result authoritatively permits replacement. Add one consumer-level conformance regression: unknown after possible commit → click original start again/reload → no fresh identity/no second mutation → reconcile exact first operation. Include multiple packs and EN/RU phone controls in follow-up validation.

## QA-68-02 — MEDIUM — Common error recovery drops retry semantics and gives misleading next actions

**Class:** confirmed presentation behavior; requirement/design gap at facade-to-consumer recovery. No backend/session-invalidation bug is inferred. **Affected:** AC-02 explicit error semantics, Projects common error state. **Status:** confirmed for controlled responses; a real expired session was not simulated.

Reproduce Projects with existing `projects-list-error`: its adapter error has `retry:'none'`, message “not available in this build.” Content nevertheless offers Retry. The injected unauthenticated variant says “Сессия завершилась. Войдите, чтобы продолжить.” but presents **Повторить**, with no direct sign-in action; the harness still supplies a valid identity snapshot deliberately, so this probes disagreement between service facts and shell observation rather than proving a real session remains authenticated.

Expected: distinguish unavailable configuration, retryable observation failure, and authentication recovery. Actual: all list failures become only a `ServiceProblemCode` in `ProjectsScreen.tsx:218-221`; `ServiceError.retry` (`services/contracts.ts:44,74`) is discarded. Lines 519-523 render the same Retry for every code. The source message/localization is clear, but the action does not match it. Repeating an observation is not itself a duplicate mutation; do not extend this finding into a transaction claim.

User impact: a user who needs sign-in or a corrected build is encouraged to repeat an action that cannot address the stated cause. On phone the relevant auth entry is also hidden in the menu. The task requires explicit outcomes but does not specify a shared recovery-action mapping or how a domain unauthenticated response reconciles identity observation; this lets consumers implement inconsistent recovery.

Scoped recommendation: define the small shared mapping from outcome/retry directive to permitted recovery action; preserve those facts in consumer state. Offer sign-in with safe return for an authentication-required state, and explanatory availability guidance when retry cannot change the build. Keep deliberate refresh for retryable reads. Validate each mapping via a controlled consumer matrix in both languages, including a real identity refresh/expiry test separately.

![Permanent unavailable response offers Retry](evidence/unavailable-en-desktop.png)
![Session-ended message offers Repeat rather than a direct sign-in action](evidence/unauthenticated-ru-390.png)

## QA-68-03 — LOW — Desktop recovery controls are visually underscaled for important decisions

**Class:** requirement/design quality concern, **not** a reference mismatch or an asserted accessibility violation. **Affected:** consumer recovery states under AC-02; shared desktop density. **Evidence:** measured and visually inspected.

At 1440×900 the primary recovery Retry is **56.06×28 CSS px, Mabry Medium 13/20**. The payment-status action is **926×28 px, 13/20**; it stretches nearly the whole content width while its tiny centered label has weak emphasis against 16px status copy. RU crosses from **113.19×48, 16/24** at 767px to **86.34×28, 13/20** at 768px. There is ample whitespace in the reviewed failure states, so compact density does little useful work here. Phone actions retain measured 48px height.

The button matches adopted BTN geometry (`button-clean.md.txt:312-319,355-368`) and shared contract compact desktop choice. The concern is product usability of applying the minimum compact treatment to recovery actions, not failure to copy the source. Retry is infrequent, but is the only local recovery action in these states; checking an uncertain payment is a consequential job. A 28px target is not automatically a WCAG failure.

Scoped recommendation: retain Mabry/palette/source treatment but consider the source 32px size or a documented larger desktop recovery role with stronger hierarchy; avoid a very wide, very shallow payment-status control. Validate at 1440×700, 767/768, 200% zoom and keyboard focus before adopting a change. Do not increase every application control indiscriminately.

![Compact desktop recovery against substantial whitespace](evidence/conflict-en-1440.png)
![At 767px phone target remains 48px](evidence/unavailable-ru-767.png)
![At 768px recovery shrinks to 28px](evidence/unavailable-ru-768.png)

## What works and reference comparison

The unavailable, conflict, loading and unconfirmed strings stay explicit and localized. No fake project rows, fabricated percentage, fake success or adapter prose leak appears in these captures. The Credits unknown notice leaves available balance at 120 and labels pending history with dashes; those values are synthetic fixture truth, not accounting proof. EN desktop and RU phone recovery content is readable with no primary-capture horizontal document overflow; Russian notices wrap cleanly. Source button shapes, white secondary surface, faint edge and 6px corner treatment are recognizable in the open Light source reference. Mabry is intentionally substituted for source Inter; full CSS-pixel shadow/crop fidelity and contrast were not comprehensively audited here.

Actual real configuration fails visibly rather than showing a mock workspace. `services/index.ts:89-91` throws before mock context construction; `main.tsx:32-35` renders RuntimeFailure. This satisfies the bounded fail-clearly purpose. Its operator-facing setting text is understandable in EN/RU, although it is not a production support journey and this review does not accept one.
